data.why: No example movie ships with the repo; a valid multi-frame TIFF cannot be produced by the text-based Write tool, so the install step runs the repo's own tests/synth.py (reused unchanged) to render a small synthetic NLS-reporter movie with known ruptures, a division and a death straight into /work/app/examples/demo_movie.tif before the server starts.

goals: Load a live-cell movie and calibrate the frame interval and pixel scale before analysis
Track every nucleus through the movie and inspect per-cell and per-frame measurement tables
Detect nuclear ruptures, tune the rupture threshold, and review image strips of individual rupture events
Quantify cell movement: path length, displacement, persistence, speed while ruptured vs intact
Identify divisions (lineage, timing, daughter symmetry) and deaths (timing, confidence, evidence)
Crop a region of interest and export its tables, annotated movie and PDF report

review.summary: The tree captures what Cell Surveillance is for: it covers calibration, tracking, rupture calling with threshold tuning, movement, fate, per-cell review, region export and recalibration. Its cited screens hold up in all ten I opened. It needs small fixes before filing: re-home History and recalibration, sharpen two labels, add shape/crowding and ruptured-vs-intact speed coverage plus three missing features, and record the checker's screen mismatch and incomplete replay.
